2. 24­52911 Recommendation to discuss and vote on the CoC Board Members.
  Alexa Dixson­Griggs, Administrative Coordinator, introduced the candidates up for the
  vote.
  Zhena McCollum introduced herself, she lives in Long Beach and works for the
  Department of Mental Health in the Administrative Office that oversees the Long
  Beach area. She has been tasked to increase collaboration and improve DMH
  resources. In addition, she has experience working with and in the City of Long
  Beach with Cabrillo Villages and the MSC.
  Co­Chair Jamies Shufford comments on Zhena introduction, he agrees with
  being able to do more collaboration to help address homelessness including
  education, mental health, and physical health.
  Hawk McFadzen was introduced, pronouns are them/they. They are the
  Research Analyst at Compton College who works in the Office of Institutional
  Effectiveness and is working on their Master’s. As well as that they currently sit
  on the Lived Experience Board and are interested in rethinking systems that are
  more person­centered to use data­informed practices and establish best
  practices for homeless services.
  The last candidate, Claude who was not in attendance at the time, showed up a
  later and introduced himself. Hawk and Claude will be co­supporting each other
  to ensure that meeting quorum for the new Lived Experience Advisory Board will
  not be an issue.
  Member Elizabeth Weithers will term out and has recommended that Nikki
  Amick, from Community Development, take her place as she currently works on
  program design and program implementation of ESG grants. Members
  approved for Nikki to replace Elizabeth.
  Vote was carried at 3:52 PM.
  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Member Washington,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:
  Yes:  10 Wee, Washington, Brezenoff, Weithers, Pezzelle, Richert, Martins,
  Chotiswatdi, Bambrick, Boyce
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Shuford, Tan, Topolewski, Wilson, Howat
3. 24­52912 Recommendation to review and debrief the 2023 Continuum of Care
  Program.
  Alexa Dixson­Griggs, Administrative Coordinator, presented.
  The 2023 Debrief from HUD was received, not much changed. The goal is to
  improve further applications. Areas in which the Long Beach CoC scored lower
  include system performance, bed utilization, and strategies to reduce exit
  destination and housing retention. This also includes updating the current
  program portfolio, which is outdated and aged, and should be expected to be a
  topic at the Board Retreat.
  Jeffrey Proctor, Homeless Services Special Projects Officer spoke on the DV
  Bonuses Score Sheet. The highlighted area presented includes DV bonuses,
  which were not granted and there was a small increase in planning. The CoC is
  scoring below the median nationally. The team is working with HUD to help
  address any concerns they must better increase the score.

4. 24­52913 Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau
  Operations Report.
  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager presented.
  There was an update on staffing for positions like the Bureau Secretary and
  Participant Engagement Specialist that will be supporting several different areas
  including the Lived Experience group (ABEL). Cassandra Bonney was
  introduced as the newest supervisor in the administrative operations division.
  Allison King is now the permanent Director of the Health department. Anna is the
  new acting Bureau Manager for the Housing Authority.
  ABEL is an advisory board with lived experience previously known as (LEAB),
  the Board has voted to change its name to ABEL­ Advisory Board with Live
  Experience.
  Onsite monitoring is underway. This year ABEL will be included in the monitoring
  process. Members will be touring the facilities before monitoring is completed.
  There was a discussion on data collection of demographics on a system level
  over the past quarter that has moved into HMIS, and staff is expecting to gather
  better insights into the inflow and outflow of people exited into permanent
  housing.
  The 2023 strategic plan was discussed and how that incorporates the ongoing
  work being done on the larger city strategic plan from everyone's home. Further
  discussion on short­ and long­term goals will be discussed at the CoC Board
  retreat.
  2024 PIT Count results are expected to be released early next month.
  Construction at the Project Homekey site formerly known as the Luxury Inn has
  begun, the prioritization will be for people who have been out there the longest
  and have a disabling condition.
  The CoC received their allocation amount from Measure H funding. The amount
  received was double last year’s allocation. Measure H is coming to a 10­year
  lifespan, there is an effort to half the .50 sales tax on the November ballot. This
  would fund affordable permanent supportive housing development through La
  Casa.
  First to Serve will start as the site operator at PHK on 1725 Long Beach Blvd.

  received was double last year’s allocation. Measure H is coming to a 10­year

  would fund affordable permanent supportive housing development through La
  Casa.
  First to Serve will start as the site operator at PHK on 1725 Long Beach Blvd.
  The County has leased a hotel in Long Beach for 3 years, with a current focus on
  Signal Hill, about 30 people from Signal Hill and 25 people from Long Beach are
  being housed. Once its current participants move into more permanent locations,
  all rooms will be prioritized through the Long Beach CES.
  Members Daniel Brezenoff commented on the increasing age of PEH, and
  senior citizens there are additional challenges with this population that include
  increased physical health needs. The staff responded in agreement.
  Board Member Shelby Bambrick asks if either Project HomeKey or Project
  Pathways offers family­related funding or housing. The staff responded that
  currently these projects are solely for individuals or coupled adults, children are
  not allowed.
  Hawk the ABEL Representative requested that the Board be patient with ABEL
  as they establish their bylaws.

  HSAC Representative Pam Chotiswatdi provided an update on the work that the
